messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: Eviction surge + streaming token cadence drops detected in region us-east-1. KV cache eviction rate = 5.2k/s, continuous-batching backlog rising, partial flush errors seen. Incident INC-2283344556 opened.
Maria: seeing it on graphs — cache working set jumped ~3x in 45s, look like a resync/pulse of large prefix entries. batch amplification visible: mean batch_size went 8→96.
Jai: that explains the memory pressure and streaming stalls. Amplified batches push kv cache evictions, which then cause repeated prefetch/resync. I'm joining.
oncall-amber: I'm on-call. quick mitigation: I've throttled continuous-batching concurrency to 2 and set batch_size_max=24. Ran: `POST /admin/ops?set=batch_size_max=24&concurrency=2` — can people confirm effect? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
SRE-Lee: graphs show backlog flattening, token cadence error rate down ~40% after the change. But we're still seeing partial flush stacktraces in streaming worker logs: `partial_flush: nil kv_ref` repeatedly.
Maria: that partial_flush nil is new — likely a race between eviction and streaming partial-flush path. Might be a bug introduced by the resync that leaves refs dangling.
Jai: I found a pattern in traces: large resync -> new prefix pages enqueued -> continuous-batch attempts to flush in-flight streaming frames while prefix not yet resident -> flush handler gets nil kv handle. Adding guard prevents crash but we need a config hotfix now.
infra-bot: Candidate hotfix branch built: `hotfix/cache-guard-2283` image: `registry/redwood:hotfix-2283-rc1` (sha256:abcd1234). Smoke tests passed locally.
support-alex: FYI two customers reported degraded streaming responses ~ 11:14 UTC: session tokens stutter, partial outputs. No data loss reported. Affected customers: beta-shop, replies.ai. Raising priority on CS side.
oncall-amber: rolling the hotfix to a single canary host in us-east-1 now (1/10). Command:
```
kubectl set image deploy/stream-worker stream-worker=registry/redwood:hotfix-2283-rc1 -n us-east-1-canary
```
Maria: while canary deploys, I recommend conservative cache backoff: `kv_prefetch.window_ms=500`, `kv_prefetch.max_pages=8` to reduce resync pressure. Pushing these via runtime flags.
Jai: small patch to guard partial flush landed in hotfix branch. Patch diff:
```
if kv_handle == nil {
  log.Warn("partial_flush: nil kv_handle, dropping flush")
  return
}
```
I also added a metric `partial_flush_dropped_total` to track frequency.
ops-bot: Canary update: 1/10 hosts updated. No regression for 60s. Eviction rate on canary host reduced, streaming stalls absent on canary.
SRE-Lee: ok - let's promote to 3/10 and keep the runtime batch limits in place while we monitor for 15m.
oncall-amber: promoting to 3/10. Command executed.
support-alex: customers notified via status page draft: "We are aware of streaming interruptions in us-east-1 related to cache resync events. Mitigation in progress; temporary throughput limits applied." Approving to send.
Maria: observed a second pulse but much smaller. partial_flush_dropped_total spiked to 73 then dropped. Batches stayed under 48.
Jai: good. create rollback plan in case we see regression after full roll: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/stream-worker --to-revision=prev` and `set batch_size_max back to 128` is our revert. Documenting in the thread.
SRE-Lee: incident impact summary for postmortem: - Root cause: bursty prefix resync (large prefix write) causing batch amplification → memory pressure → eviction → streaming partial flush races. - Mitigations applied: batch_size_max lowered, concurrency throttled, hotfix guard deployed to canary then ramped, cache prefetch backoff. - Customer impact: intermittent streaming stalls and partial outputs for limited customers in us-east-1; no integrity/data loss. - Next actions: permanent fix to partial_flush ordering, add prefetch pacing, add autosafe to prevent batch amplification > 64, run traffic replay to validate.
ops-bot: Promotion status: 3/10 -> 8/10 in progress. No new errors reported on promoted hosts.
oncall-amber: full rollout complete to all targets (10/10) at ts=2283344586. Eviction rate back to baseline.
Jai: creating a postmortem draft and will assign action items: reorder flush path + stronger handle lifecycle checks + add synthetic test to simulate resync pulses.
Maria: tagging infra/kv and eng-runtime for follow-up. Good work team. :tada:
support-alex: status page update published at 2283344589. I'll follow up with impacted customer list and an outreach plan.
ops-bot: INC-2283344556 resolved (mitigation complete). Archive will be created for postmortem generation.
